subtopics: Selecting and Configuring a Compiler Version
learning_outcomes: Explain Selecting and Configuring a Compiler Version and relate it to the contract execution model.
Analyze or implement a small Solidity example involving Selecting and Configuring a Compiler Version.
Test at least one normal case and one edge, failure, security, or version-compatibility case.

content.intro: This lesson turns the syllabus topic “Selecting and Configuring a Compiler Version” into a small, inspectable example. You will work from an expected behavior, run a local check, and record the assumptions behind the result.
content.why_it_matters: A version declaration constrains which compiler versions accept a source file; it does not pin external build tools or network behavior by itself. Pin the actual compiler in your build, read the relevant release notes and bug list, and reproduce the build before release.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Separate the editor and compiler from the local chain, wallet, test suite, and deployment configuration. Build and test locally before using a remote network.

items.text: For this lesson, explain the term in your own words, identify where it affects contract behavior, and note one assumption or edge case to test.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: 1. Predict how the example should behave in relation to Selecting and Configuring a Compiler Version. 2. Compile it with the pinned compiler and inspect warnings. 3. Test one normal case and one boundary or failure case in a local EVM. 4. Record what the result demonstrates and what it does not establish about production safety.

content_blocks.expected_output: A successful build should emit ABI and bytecode artifacts; exact bytecode depends on the pinned compiler and build settings.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Open a local Remix workspace or a pinned Foundry/Hardhat project, select compiler 0.8.37, compile the snippet, deploy it only to a local VM, and call greet(). CodeLeaf does not execute Solidity in its browser preview.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Reset the local VM or restart the test fixture, redeploy the example, and repeat the same tests. Restore the original compiler, optimizer, and EVM-target settings before comparing results. Never add keys or other secrets to source files.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: A snippet that compiles is not automatically correct or secure. Check the selected compiler version, read every warning, assert preconditions, test reverting and edge cases, and inspect external-call assumptions. If a tool or opcode is unsupported, verify the compiler release and target-chain support instead of weakening checks.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Extend the small example to demonstrate Selecting and Configuring a Compiler Version. Write down the expected result before running it, add a normal test and a failure/boundary test, then note one design trade-off or security concern.

content_blocks.title: Recap and next step
content_blocks.text: Recap: Selecting and Configuring a Compiler Version should be understood alongside the module principle: Separate the editor and compiler from the local chain, wallet, test suite, and deployment configuration. Build and test locally before using a remote network. Continue to the next lesson only after you can explain the behavior, reproduce the result locally, and state the important limitations.

content.task: Create a small local-only example that demonstrates Selecting and Configuring a Compiler Version. Define a normal case and a boundary/failure case, predict the result, test both, and explain one limitation. Do not deploy this teaching exercise with real funds.
task_acceptance_criteria: State the expected behavior before testing and describe the observed result.
Include a repeatable test or manual trace covering a boundary or failure case.
Document one assumption, security concern, or version constraint rather than claiming production readiness.
hints: Start with the simplest behavior related to Selecting and Configuring a Compiler Version and make the input and expected result explicit.
Change one condition or input at a time and rerun the same test to isolate the effect.
Read compiler warnings and error details; do not treat deployment success as a security review.
content.expected_output: A successful build should emit ABI and bytecode artifacts; exact bytecode depends on the pinned compiler and build settings.
troubleshooting: Confirm that the compiler version is 0.8.37 and that build settings are recorded.
For a revert, inspect the precondition and test both allowed and denied inputs.
For external calls or network-specific features, confirm the local chain's behavior and the target-network assumptions.
